attributes.provenance: Fleet worker AL2, work_claim.alias-world.20260831.v1, worktree GDL-Claude-AliasWorld. Four functions, three TUs, ten probed source variants, all measured with probe.py --ops against clean banked baselines and all reverted: items.c::AddLocatorInstList (4 variants), items.c::LinkTriggerToCam (1), gauntworld.c::fn_80062A00 (3), screensaver.c::draw_inventory_panel (5, of which 2 were member-form). The positive control is items.c::GetMilestonePos, already byte-exact, whose `sItemRuntime.milestones[idx].matrix[12]` emits precisely `mulli r5,r3,104 / lis+addi -> r0 / add r3,r0,r5 / lfs f0,15940(r3)`.
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies whenever a target stream shows `add rX,rBase,rIdx` followed by a large immediate displacement (lfs/stfs/lwz/stw/lwzu K(rX)) and the reconstruction instead emits `addi rIdx,rIdx,K` plus an indexed x-form (lfsx/stfsx/lwzx/stwx) or a plain displacement off a cached element pointer. Boundary/cost refinement of claim.law.cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base and a documented CONFLICT with claim.law.whole-fn-address-cache.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC canonicalizes an address of the form base + index + K to base + (index + K) and discards the source's written associativity, EXCEPT when the base is a global SYMBOL reached through a member/array reference, where the constant is symbol-relative and instead folds into the memory operand's displacement, leaving `add rX,rBase,rIdx`. The complete tested matrix (base kind x access kind) has exactly one flipping cell: (1) pointer LOCAL + member access `p->arr[i].f` gives addi+x-form (AddLocatorInstList loop 2 and case 7); (2) pointer LOCAL + raw offset `*(T*)(p + off + K)` gives addi+x-form (fn_80062A00, LinkTriggerToCam); (3) global SYMBOL + raw offset `*(T*)(sGlobal + off + K)` ALSO gives addi+x-form - byte-for-byte identical to (2), so casting the symbol is not enough (fn_80062A00 variant B2); (4) global SYMBOL + member access `sGlobal.arr[i].f` or `&sGlobal.arr[i]` is the ONLY form that yields target's `add`+displacement. Writing the constant last in the source (`(base + i*STRIDE) + offsetof(...)`, even with explicit parentheses) changes NOTHING - AddLocatorInstList variant A4 was byte-identical to the unmodified baseline - so operand order is a dead axis and should never be probed for this residual. THE TAX, and why this is usually a losing trade: form (4) also makes MWCC re-materialize the symbol address with a fresh lis/addi pair PER REGION (per loop nest, and per basic block in an if-chain) instead of holding one cached base register, because the local pointer variable that claim.law.whole-fn-address-cache prescribes for exactly that purpose is the alias whose removal form (4) requires - and MWCC never CSEs a direct symbol reference with a live local copy of that same address (claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges). Measured costs: AddLocatorInstList full conversion 3 materializations, real 306->400; per-site partial 2 surplus, real 320 but --ops target-only reached NONE (the best structural state, still rejected on the monotonic-result rule); LinkTriggerToCam 6 surplus over nine `if` blocks, real 82->126 with instruction count going 119 (exact) -> 131; draw_inventory_panel 5 surplus, real 547->611. Targets that show BOTH one lis/addi and per-access adds are therefore NOT reachable by respelling alone. PROCEDURE: before spending builds on this residual, count the target's lis/addi pairs for the symbol. If target has one cached base AND per-access adds, the residual is rematerialize-vs-cache register allocation - classify REGISTER_ONLY, record, and move to the function's structural residuals (branch shape, declared-local count, spill set) which are what actually drive MWCC's cost decision. Only spend the conversion when the target itself re-materializes the base per region, or when the function is small enough that one region covers every site. Corollary confirming claim.law.cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base's own all-or-nothing warning from the opposite direction: in fn_80062A00, deleting the cached alias was NEUTRAL three times over because MWCC's GCSE simply re-formed the identical base+index web and promoted it to a callee-saved register (target saved 10 GPRs in a 120-byte frame, ours 11 in a 128-byte frame, the extra register BEING the web) - source-level alias deletion cannot beat GCSE, only a different addressing FORM can.
